newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB lifts Australia wheat estimate to 21.5 mt.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB lifts Australia wheat estimate to 21.5 mt.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Monday it raised its forecast for the 1996/97 wheat harvest to 21.5 million tonnes from 21.0 million tonnes previously.
The AWB also said it had left unchanged at A$185 per tonne its pool estimate return price for benchmark Australian Standard White (ASW) wheat.
The AWB said the increase confirms the 1996/97 harvest will be at least Australia's second largest crop on record. The record crop was 22 million tonnes in 1983/84.
The upward revision brings the AWB forecast closer in line with that of private forecaster Australian Wheat Forecasters Pty, which expects a crop of 21.8 million tonnes.
The AWB also lifted its estimate of returns for durum wheat numbers 1 and 2 delivered to pool by A$15.00 to A$225.00 and A$240.00 a tonne, respectively.
The estimate for durum number 3 has been lifted by A$35.00 a tonne to A$220.00 a tonne following some good sales to Europe, the AWB said. All other grades were left unchanged.

"Just over 12 million tonnes has now been delivered to the AWB pools, and we're yet to see any regular yield pattern emerge," the AWB'a general manager of merchandising, Ron Storey said in a statement.
"This is a crop that has surprised everyone, as in late October the best estimates put the crop size at 19.5 million tonnes and now we're within a half-million tonnes of a record crop," he said.
Conclusion of Australia's deal to sell one million tonnes of wheat to India last week and "anticipation that we'll soon resume sales to Iraq" underpin the current pool estimate price, Storey said.
He also said a significant amount of on-farm storage existed in Australia and that it was difficult to gauge precisely how much wheat producers will retain on-farm for future trading.
"I'm urging them to remember that the returns from this pool have the potential to remain volatile for a much longer period of time than we've seen in the last 10 years," he said.
The AWB's next scheduled date to release any pool estimate revisions is January 6, 1997, the AWB said.
